newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE RUBBER FUTURES CLOSE LOWER ACROSS BOARD.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE RUBBER FUTURES CLOSE LOWER ACROSS BOARD.

text.p: Singapore rubber futures closed lower across the board in moderate trade on Thursday on some late local selling interest in line with lower Japanese prices, brokers said.
Prices in Tokyo and Kobe also closed lower across the board, reflecting the yen's stronger tone against the U.S. dollar.

A statement by the Indonesian central bank that it will no longer announce its daily intervention/conversion bands had little impact on the market. Traders said the managed float of the rupiah may help Indonesian producers, but was offset by weak demand due to the holidays in the U.S., Europe and Japan.

"The morning session was quiet and featureless on lack of fresh factors. But prices were marked down slightly in the afternoon on some local selling interest in sympathy with weaker prices in Tokyo and Kobe," a local broker said.
The rubber trade was also waiting for direction from Japan and the major rubber consumers like Bridgestone, which was said to have bought some TSR20 rubber yesterday.
At around 0945 GMT, October RSS3 fell 2.25 cents to 92.75 U.S. cents a kg.
